entries.title: The new version is the app now
entries.use: When you open Grining Pens: you land on the new version, at the usual addresses, and the old one is gone from the way. If you need the old one for something: Settings, The old version (it lives under /prev/ for a while). Old /next/ links still work. The new version also got what only the old one had: Edit this fill on a pen's page, the next pens to ink under Ink next on the desk, a pen's filling and year in the list (P0 to P3 on its tile), samples, years and MoI links on inks, the timeline's 2x and 4x zoom, inks and ink spending per year in Stats, Cupboard, and Year by year in Stats. Pens and Inks remember the list or the grid.

entries.title: supen and suink in the app
entries.use: When you want the terminal's supen or suink table on your phone: in the new version open More, then Turns: supen, suink (or press Ctrl-K and type supen). Each rotation is a table of its pens: how many fills, how many days inked, and the days since the last fill ended, green while in turn, amber near it, red past it. A pen inked now shows its ink. Inks shows the same for the open bottles. The chips pick one rotation (Out is supen -r out) and the order. The desk's "past their turn" opens it too.

entries.title: Every pen has a photo
entries.use: When you open a pen that never had a photo: it has one now, found on the web and, for most, cleaned up onto the same paper as your own shots. A few are drawn from the pen's name, and the note under the photo says so. To check them: in the new version, open the desk's photo badge, or Pens, Pens needing a photo. Tap Right if it is your pen. Tap Wrong if it is not: the photo goes, and the next search tries another one.

entries.title: A new version to try
entries.use: When you want to see the collection as ink: open More, then The new version (or Settings, Try the new version). The desk shows each inked pen with a swab of its real ink colour, how long it has been in, and what to ink next. Inks are a wall of swatch cards. Stats is new: a river of every fill since the first, what you own against what you use, whether each pen earns its keep, and whether the rotation keeps up. Everything can be edited there too, and it is the same data. Settings there can make it the version the app opens with, or take you back.

entries.title: Charts of your inkings
entries.use: When you wonder how often you ink up, and with what: open History, then Inkings. It shows your inkings per year in ink colours, a square for each month, how many pens were inked at once, how long a fill stays, your colours and your most used pens and inks. Tap a chip to see one year. Tap a bar or a square for its numbers, and See them opens those inkings. A pen's and an ink's own page now show their inkings per year too.

entries.title: Put Grining Pens on your home screen
entries.use: When you open the collection in a phone's browser: a few seconds in, a bar above the tab bar offers to add Grining Pens to your home screen, where it opens full screen like an app. Tap Install (on an iPhone: Share, then Add to Home Screen), or tap the cross and it stays away for two weeks. Settings, Install does the same at any time.

entries.title: One bar on a big screen
entries.use: When you browse the collection on a computer: everything sits in one bar at the top. Your places are tabs (Desk, Inkings, Pens, Inks, History, Records); on Pens and Inks, Filter opens the rotation or colour chips under it; the magnifier searches pens and inks; the three dots open the menu. On a pen or an ink page its actions (Edit, Share, Delete) are buttons you can see. On a phone each list now says at the top how many there are and when you last inked a pen.

entries.title: Search your inkings
entries.use: When you want to know when a pen last held an ink: open Inkings and type in the box at the top, for example "custom 74 blue". Every word must match the pen, the ink or the nib, and accents do not matter. The long lists (pens, inks, inkings) now show 50 at a time: tap Load more at the bottom for the next ones.

entries.title: Pull down to reload
entries.use: When Grining Pens on your phone's home screen shows something old: pull the page down from the top and let go, and it loads again. After a new version goes live, a "New version ready" note waits above the tab bar; tap Refresh when it suits you.

entries.title: Photos open full screen
entries.use: When you want to see a nib, a finish or a swatch up close: tap a pen's photo, an ink's swatch or a writing sample. Pinch or double-tap to zoom, drag to look around, swipe sideways for the next one, and flick down or press Back to close.
